newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albania ruling party urges counter-demo Tuesday.
newsitem.headline: Albania ruling party urges counter-demo Tuesday.

text.p: Albania's ruling right-wing Democrats on Monday called for a counter-demonstration outside the party headquarters of rival Socialists for Tuesday in a move unlikely to ease tension in the Balkan state.

Foreign Minister Tritan Shehu, chairman of the Democratic Party, told a tense meeting of supporters in Tirana that it was time for the party to show its muscle against what he called "red gangs" of former communist secret police.
Shehu accused left-wingers of inflaming two weeks of protests around the country sparked by the collapse of pyramid savings schemes.
"I invite you to gather tomorrow in front of Socialist Party headquarters...to protest peacefully against the leaders of this party," Shehu told some 700 chanting supporters.
Democratic Party backers shouted "We love the president" and "Down with communism, down with the red bastards".
Shehu urged Democrat activists across the country to "wake up from your lethargy and...peacefully demonstrate against those who want to destroy democracy in Albania".

While Shehu urged supporters to gather peacefully on Tuesday, the presence of Democrats outside rival party headquarters near central Skanderbeg Square was likely to be seen as provocative given the tense situation.

The Socialist Party, reformed successor of the hardline communist party, called for a peaceful protest in Tirana on Sunday but the demonstration turned violent when around 2,000 people clashed with riot police.
Police used batons and water cannon to disperse the crowd.
A wave of protests has spread in the south of the impoverished nation where thousands had poured large sums of cash into one failed investment scheme popular in the area.
Angry crowds set ablaze offices of the ruling Democratic Party, as well as town halls, courts and other buildings.

Shehu, who was himself attacked by an angry mob in the town of Lushnje on Saturday, criticised some Democrat activists for not protecting party headquarters set ablaze on Sunday in the southern towns of Berat, Korca, Vlora, and Fieri.

"One should know that nobody can attack (Democratic Party) buildings, which are the symbol of victory over communism in Albania," he said, blaming some activists for not defending the buildings with their blood.
Tirana's Democratic Party mayor Albert Brojka accused the opposition of inciting people to set fire to buildings.

"The same forces impoverished and destroyed Albania for 50 years...They should not been allowed to rule the country again," Brojka said, adding that the government, the ruling party and police had been too tolerant.
Shehu dismissed calls for leftist parties to be banned but urged Socialists to distance themselves from their leaders.
The meeting welcomed a decision by parliament to invest special powers in Democrat President Sali Berisha enabling him to use the military to restore order.
"Long live the commander of the armed forces," some activists shouted at the meeting.

At a separate meeting in Tirana, opposition Socialists, Social Democrats and Democratic Alliance called for talks with all political parties to try to resolve the crisis and stressed that all protests should be non-violent.
But opposition leaders also called for the resignation of the government of Prime Minister Aleksander Meksi.
